text:
maya: Quick bring-up summary from the mini-sample run for the new 11B candidate. ran fp16 / int8 / int4 on a 2k-sample slice (mix of chat + longform).
diego: nice, numbers?
maya: TL;DR — int8 looks like the best default for GTN: ~35% cost savings vs fp16, <0.7% delta on our primary quality metric. int4 gives ~60% cost savings but quality drop is around 2% and more variance on longform.
alex: can you paste the micro-metrics? even ballpark is fine for product to decide.
maya: sure — aggregate numbers (per 1M tokens): fp16 baseline cost = $1.00 (index), int8 = $0.65, int4 = $0.40. latency P95 (single-turn): fp16=220ms, int8=180ms, int4=160ms. CPU overhead for deserializing kv cache negligible.
sophia: what about pass/fail on the eval set? any regressions on targeted slices?
maya: primary eval (QA F1 weighted): fp16=0.842, int8=0.837 (-0.6%), int4=0.824 (-2.1%). longform coherence metric dropped more for int4 (~3.5% on convo-length>800 tokens).
nora: interesting — int8 is within our usual noise band. how consistent across prompts?
maya: across 10 quick priming prompts: int8 median delta -0.5%, 90th pctile -1.1%. int4 median -1.8%, 90th pctile -3.2%.
diego: that's promising. product will ask: what to ship as default and what guardrails?
alex: my vote: default routing to int8 for low-cost tiers, fallback to fp16 for high-accuracy routes (e.g., official answers / billing-related flows). set canary fraction to 5% then ramp to 25% over a week if no signal.
sophia: agree. add automatic rollback if eval-signal drops >1.2% on our core eval set or we see >0.5% increase in human-reported regressions.
maya: ops-bot, can you create a canary job per alex's plan?
ops-bot: created canary job: /canary run new-11b-int8 -> targets: 5% traffic, collect routing:priming-slice, metric hooks: QA_F1, Longform_Coh, latency_p95. job id 2026-6789-canary.
nora: what about A/B scoring windows? product wants to show unit econ impact to GTN.
maya: quick calc we shared with finance: expected unit-econ per 1M tokens served (weighted mix): fp16 = $1.00 cost -> estimated price->margin X, int8 = $0.65 -> saves $0.35/1M, int4 saves $0.60/1M. projecting monthly traffic of 500M tokens, int8 saves ~$175k/mo, int4 ~$300k/mo but with quality risk.
diego: product should see both the econ and the risk delta. propose GTN guidance: "use int8 for conversational defaults. enable int4 only behind an explicit opt-in flag for non-critical bulk workloads (embeddings/batch summarization)."
sophia: add rollout notes: 1) small canary (5%), 2) compare automated eval each day, 3) manual spot-checks on flagged failed prompts, 4) after 7 days and stable, 25% for 48h, then 100% if ok.
alex: also include a fallback policy: if traffic experiences >2x error rate or latency p95 regresses >30% on routed machines, fallback to fp16 immediately.
maya: action items: I will prod detailed priming slices and the 2k sample csv -> drive eval dashboards. diego -> compile short GTN one-pager with the unit econ numbers and recommended flags. nora -> schedule a 30m review with product next Tue.
nora: ack, will schedule.
ops-bot: note: metric hooks already wired to dashboards/alerts for canary job 2026-6789-canary.
maya: one more note — we saw specific failure modes in int4 for factual recall on numeric tables; add numeric-table sub-slice to signal set before broad int4 rollouts.
diego: good catch. we'll add an assert in the eval pipeline for numeric-table recall >= baseline -1.0% for int4 to be considered.
sophia: perfect. if the canary stays green, we can push the int8 default for GTN next Friday. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks everyone — short and actionable. closing thread unless anything else pops up.
